blogs.title: When Angioedema Isn't: The Critical Role of CK in Unexplained Neck Swelling
blogs.description: This post challenges the reflexive workup of 'idiopathic angioedema' in the ED. We analyze a case where severe neck swelling mimicked Ludwig's angina and allergic reactions, yet the key diagnostic pivot was recognizing non-pitting edema inconsistent with bradykinin/histamine pathways. Learn why ordering a Creatine Kinase (CK) level should be mandatory in any patient with unexplained cervical edema accompanied by even subtle proximal weakness or nailfold changes, preventing dangerous delays in diagnosing inflammatory myopathies like dermatomyositis.

blogs.title: Beyond Gottron's Papules: Decoding Subtle Cutaneous Clues in Anti-SAE1 Dermatomyositis
blogs.description: Classic teaching emphasizes Heliotrope rash and Gottron's papules, but what happens when they are absent? This article dives into the specific phenotype of Anti-SAE1 antibody-positive dermatomyositis, which often presents with prominent subcutaneous edema ('pseudoangioedema') and minimal classic rash. We review how to spot low-yield physical exam findings like periungual telangiectasias, holster sign, and nonspecific facial erythema that can unlock the diagnosis before catastrophic muscle breakdown occurs.

blogs.title: The Airway Threat You Can't Intubate Away: Managing Dysphagia and Aspiration in Acute Myositis
blogs.description: While we worry about laryngeal edema in angioedema, this case highlights a different airway catastrophe: profound pharyngeal muscle weakness leading to silent aspiration and respiratory failure. We discuss the pathophysiology of bulbar involvement in dermatomyositis, the limitations of standard ENT evaluations (like flexible nasendoscopy) in detecting dynamic swallowing failures, and the urgent need for early video fluoroscopic swallow studies and aggressive immunosuppression to preserve airway protection.

blogs.title: Steroids Alone Aren't Enough: Navigating Escalated Immunosuppression in Severe Dermatomyositis
blogs.description: With CK levels exceeding 16,000 U/L and life-threatening dysphagia, this case illustrates the necessity of rapid, multi-agent induction therapy beyond high-dose corticosteroids. We break down the rationale for combining IVIG, Rituximab, and Mycophenolate Mofetil in severe anti-SAE1 cases, discussing agent selection based on comorbidities (such as avoiding methotrexate in potential lung disease) and managing complex prophylaxis needs like PJP prevention in heavily immunosuppressed patients.

blogs.title: The Malignancy Shadow: Risk Stratification and Screening Protocols for New-Onset Dermatomyositis
blogs.description: A new diagnosis of dermatomyositis carries a significant risk of underlying paraneoplastic malignancy, particularly with specific antibody profiles. Using this case as a framework, we outline the IMACS guidelines for cancer screening, explaining how factors like male sex, dysphagia, and Anti-SAE1 positivity elevate risk stratification. The post provides a practical checklist for emergency physicians and hospitalists on initiating appropriate age-and-risk-adjusted cancer surveillance immediately upon diagnosis.
